claims.statement: Social feedback such as likes/comments can function as a reward signal that changes subsequent social-media behavior; experimental manipulations support causal effects of feedback/reward rate on later posting or sharing.
Reward-learning/value-updating processes can shape the timing or probability of subsequent social-media posting/sharing behavior.
A social-media post/share creates an opportunity for social feedback when other users can react; feedback is conditional on audience/platform response.

Real-world social-media posting can reflect a mixture of reinforcement learning and habitual processes, with substantial individual differences; posting frequency or repetition alone must not be used as a habit diagnosis.
